findings.title: Inherited Bash functions and PATH can replace verification and the three external launch sites
findings.evidence: The runner does not clear exported functions or normalize PATH before unqualified sha256sum/awk/grep/find/sort/xargs/env/mv calls; env -i is itself resolved as an unqualified command.
findings.impact: Zero, extra, or fabricated license/VCS/simv activity and fabricated hashes/seals remain possible despite the literal one/one/one source shape.
findings.required_fix: Use a clean fixed launcher and absolute helper paths, reject inherited shell functions/environment hooks, and statically bind the only three EDA launches.

findings.title: The sealed review does not authorize the exact live runner identity
findings.evidence: M1894 checks caller-provided runner and review hashes independently and greps only PASS/count lines; it never compares a reviewed_runner_sha256 field with the live runner hash.
findings.impact: A modified runner can be caller-self-pinned while reusing an independent PASS review of another source identity.
findings.required_fix: Require one exact audited runner SHA from the sealed review and compare it to the live runner; release/audit must pin the same review and runner pair.

findings.title: mv -T -n publication has no moved-source and sealed-destination postcondition
findings.evidence: Lines 63 and 149 use mv -T -n; GNU mv -n may return zero after declining replacement. Lines 150 onward assume publication succeeded without checking that WORK disappeared or RESULT/FAILURE is the moved sealed directory.
findings.impact: The runner can announce raw success or suppress quarantine handling while the authoritative destination was not published by this attempt.
findings.required_fix: Use an atomic no-replace primitive with an unambiguous result, then verify source absence, destination identity, and both seals before changing WORK_ACTIVE or printing success.

findings.title: Post-attempt failure sealing and publication errors are ignored
findings.evidence: on_exit executes seal_dir WORK || true and mv ... FAILURE || true.
findings.impact: A license/compile/sim failure is not guaranteed to yield the promised sealed non-retry quarantine.
findings.required_fix: Make the failure terminal state explicit and verified; if the primary quarantine cannot be sealed/published, retain a durable secondary failure marker without reporting a sealed quarantine.

findings.title: Same-UID collision gate omits the 15-byte procfs name for common_shell_exec
findings.evidence: Linux /proc/PID/comm truncates common_shell_exec to common_shell_ex; the blocked list contains common_shell_exec and common_shell_exe but not common_shell_ex.
findings.impact: A live Synopsys common-shell process can coexist with the unique M1894 attempt contrary to the exclusion contract.
findings.required_fix: Block common_shell_ex and preferably use a global same-UID EDA launch lock in addition to a procfs snapshot.

findings.title: VCS source resolution depends on the caller current directory
findings.evidence: REPO_ROOT is computed but unused, while all four filelist entries are repository-relative.
findings.impact: A valid invocation outside the repository root can consume the sole attempt and fail source resolution.
findings.required_fix: cd to the pinned REPO_ROOT before compile or generate an absolute frozen filelist.

findings.title: Partial attempt setup can consume the latch before terminal failure handling becomes active
findings.evidence: mkdir creates LOCK/ATTEMPT/WORK together, ATTEMPT is sealed, and only then WORK_ACTIVE becomes one.
findings.impact: A partial mkdir or attempt-seal failure can leave an attempt with neither a sealed success nor failure namespace.
findings.required_fix: Establish work/failure handling before consuming the attempt and verify each creation step with explicit rollback-free terminal semantics.

disposition: M1894 is not launchable. Preserve it and this review as failed source-review evidence; author an additive successor and obtain a new different-author source review before any license query, attempt, VCS, or simv execution.
